It's 8:59. The bell rings in one minute. And you're still in the hallway.
Then you find a small button in your pocket. You press it.
And everything stops. The ball in the air. Your teacher, mid-sentence.
Okay. This is the best day of my life.
So, what if you could pause time?
Rules. You can pause the world as long as you want. But every minute it's paused, you get one minute older.
At first, it's amazing. You copy the answers. You fix your hair. You eat your friend's cookie.
At home, you pause before every test. Ten minutes here. An hour there.
And here's something real. Clocks on GPS satellites run about thirty-eight microseconds faster every day than clocks on Earth.
Without fixing that, your phone's map would be off by kilometers.
Then one morning, you look in the mirror. And there's a gray hair.
Wait. How long have I been paused?
You add it up. Almost a whole year. Nobody else noticed.
So you decide. No more pausing. You press the button one last time, to unpause.
Nothing happens. The world stays frozen. And somewhere, a clock starts ticking. Just for you.
